column1: # How each archived design works, one line each, hand-edited: design (file stem)<TAB>how it works.
# Read by `mctas door gallery` and `door montage` (captions), `door leaderboard` (the line under each board
# leader) and `door catalog` (the "how" column of archive/README.md). A design missing here falls back to its
# records.tsv row, then to its track. Add a row when a new design tops a board.

column2: agent speed, built for ticks instead of blocks: the top-middle block leaves into its exit cell first, a pusher shoves a sticky puller into that exit, the puller and a fixed piston above it pull the center out in two quick moves (1-tick pulses), and the close runs it backwards with spits; opens in 12 ticks, closes in 14

agent fresh-c, "symmetric control": open and close run the SAME signal chain at the same delays, so there is no hold at all: an observer on the lever pulses the center piston A 2 ticks after each flip (swallowed on open, it pushes the center down on close), the shuttle piston Q is the lever through one repeater (its redstone block powers A at rest, then the right piston, which drags the top-middle block out), and the B window fires on both edges but is harmlessly blocked on close; fc2 makes the left pusher a pull-type pulse piston west of its backbone, fired by two observers off the lever (opens in 24 ticks, closes in 9)

agent fresh-c, "symmetric control": the same signal chain at the same delays on both lever edges (A pulsed 2 ticks after each flip, Q = the lever through one repeater, a B window that is harmlessly blocked on close), so no hold at all
agent fresh-c: fc2 with the B window fed straight off the lever, open 22 / close 9 (the floor of the symmetric family: open = b + 12 with b >= 10)

agent fresh-b, "mirrored pump": the bottom door row is glued to a slime row and pumped from below the door, the center exits upward, and the moves are triggered by the side structures' own motion (flags riding them) instead of delay lines; mp8's pump repeater fires the pump directly. Also the fastest small solid door: opens and closes in 16 ticks
agent fresh-b: the mirrored pump (mp6) with a shorter pump path; opens and closes in 16 ticks
agent fresh-b, "mirrored pump": bottom row on a slime row pumped from below the door, the center exits upward, motion-triggered by flags on the side structures; opens and closes in 16 ticks
agent fresh-b: a 45-block variant of the mirrored pump mp6

agent riders: rb6-bmobs (47) without its 7-block silent hold: a redstone block riding the left structure lands under the shuttle piston Q while the left column is open and keeps it powered; the left piston is held by a second B-window repeater, so the left structure only comes back after the close dance (closes in 23 ticks instead of 25)

agent riders: fc2 with the left piston next to X's floor, so X's three pulses per lever edge toggle it (an odd number of pulses toggles a pulse-driven piston once); fc2's two observers for it become two slimes (opens in 24 ticks, closes in 26)

agent wire21: a new family, mech-synth's 21-block pulse-only mechanism: every piston retracted at rest and fired by 2-tick pulses, one 9-pulse train identical on both lever edges (no shuttle, no hold, no torch), T leaves north above the walkway; a redstone lamp makes the right piston's last pulse late

agent slime-free, no slime or honey anywhere: logic-min's slime-free 50 (each side column on sticky pistons retracted at rest, fired by observer pulses; the right column fed by an observer + dust; a torch quasi-powers the top piston) combined with this track's left side, where the top-left door block goes UP into a puller fired by an observer chain, and a B-chain link re-grown by `door grow`

agent logic-min, no slime or honey anywhere: each side column stands on 3 sticky pistons, retracted at rest and fired by 2-tick observer pulses (a short pulse pulls a block on open, pushes it back and lets go on close); the right observer fires straight into the right pistons' dust (on close the top piston and the left column move once more before settling)

agent wire19sf, no slime or honey: mech-synth's 19-block mechanism (every edge block on its own pull-type sticky piston, the bottom-middle pulled down, the A/B elevator, a T piston) driven by ONE pulse train identical on both lever edges; the bottom-middle's trigger is a 4-block redstone-lamp circuit found by `door synth`
agent lamp-sweep, no slime or honey: wire19sf's w42 re-synthesized with time-shaping blocks in the palette: 2 stones and a cross dust replace a lamp, its floor and 2 observers

agent lamp-sweep, flat (every block in the door's plane), no slime or honey: flat's 49 (the 19-block mechanism in one plane) re-synthesized: a redstone lamp and dust replace 4 observers, after which a chain collapses into dust

agent flat-b, flat and slime-free: the 19-block mechanism upside down in the door's plane (the center goes down to an elevator below the door, the top pair is pulled up), its top chain re-synthesized by `door resynth`

agent flat: the first flat doors: the 19-block slime-free mechanism with every block in the door's plane, observer chains instead of dust (repeaters cannot be locked in one plane), then `door synth` and `door resynth` on the late chains; the lever on its observer fires all three right pistons

agent gravity, all 9 door blocks are sand: side columns on slime backbones pushed open by the doorway-floor pistons; the middle column stands on a 3-piston tower in a shaft under the door. Since g8 the middle piston S2 is retracted at rest and fired by an observer that rides the slime chain (so the close sequences itself), and g10 feeds the bottom piston's repeater from the floor of an existing dust

agent gravity: the drop tower with its middle piston S2 retracted at rest and fired by an observer riding the slime chain, so the close sequences itself; opens in 5 ticks, closes in 11 (fastest open + close at the time)
agent synth: gravity's g10 (the sand drop tower) with 3 of its sub-circuits rebuilt smaller by `door resynth`; opens in 5 ticks

agent gravity-2: a cheaper drop tower: the top tower piston is the right door column's rest support above a chain at x = 2, the right backbone ends over a fixed obsidian, and its trigger (2 observers + 1 block) was found by `door synth`; opens in 5 ticks, closes in 16

agent mechanics, fastest solid door (open 16, close 17): mechanics' 47 (bottom-middle piston fired by an observer) plus redstone-block rb9's second-pulse route (an observer on the lever and a delay line into R_B: B moves twice, at ticks 4..6 and 8..12); the minimizer's swaps then turned three dust + floor pairs into single blocks

agent top-control on search-tool's 43: the redstone-block family with a sculk sensor and one repeater as the late hold, and the bottom-middle piston retracted at rest, fired by an observer watching the bottom-right door block
agent sculk-2: st43 with its 5-block lever-to-R_B chain replaced by one calibrated sculk sensor (active 10 ticks, wakes floor(distance) ticks after each flip)
agent sculk-2: s1 with the left pusher moved so that its retracting base blocks an early pull; works facing north or south only (breaks turned 90 degrees)
agent sculk-2: a twin of s4 (the left pusher's retracting base blocks an early pull); works facing north or south only (breaks turned 90 degrees)

agent gravity, all 9 door blocks are sand: the side columns ride slime backbones pushed open by sticky pistons that are the doorway floor; the middle column stands on a 3-piston tower in a shaft under the door that collapses top-down (the sand drops 3 cells) and lifts it back bottom-up; g6 hangs the first torch under a dust (-2 from g4)

agent search-tool's local search on gravity's g6 (49): an obsidian block and a repeater became one observer, then removals (-3). The door itself is g6's: sand side columns on slime backbones pushed open by the doorway-floor pistons, the sand middle column dropping into a 3-piston shaft under the door and lifted back
agent gravity, the "drop tower": sand side columns pushed open by floor pistons, the sand middle column falls into a 3-piston shaft under the door; opens in 5 ticks

agent redstone-block, the rb family tuned for speed: a second observer on the lever moves the B window to ticks 4..12, and the hold's last repeater powers Q from behind so its falling edge updates Q at once (open 16, close 17)

agent redstone-block: rb8 through the speed-constrained minimizer (`door minimize --max-open 16 --max-close 17`): one repeater gone, another moved next to the observer's dust line; as fast as rb8 with 10 fewer blocks
agent redstone-block: first fast rb door, the B window moved from ticks 10..18 to 4..12 by a second observer watching the lever (open 16, close 19)
agent redstone-block: rb2 with a silent BUD hold for Q instead of the 24gt chain
agent top-control: the observer-fired bottom-middle piston (as in rb6-bmobs) on mechanics' rb5-hold (48)
agent mechanics: the minimizer removed a stray floor from its 91 (the 88 had landed first)
agent speed: T leaves first, a pusher shoves a sticky puller into T's exit cell, two quick pulls take the center out; F waits armed (a BUD) and a one-repeater silent hold closes it in 7 ticks

agent speed-2: the speed track's o7 without Q's hold and with an odd-tick pulse (a repeater reading a moved redstone block, a note block and an observer): the first solid door to open in 10 ticks (closes in 7)

agent lamp-sweep: speed-2's a1m (123) re-synthesized under `--max-open 10 --max-close 7`: 16 replacements (target taps, a redstone lamp and an observer for a block and 2 observers, the note block of the odd-pulse trick folded into the lamp); the fastest solid door, 16 blocks smaller (open 10, close 7)

agent fast-clean: lamp-sweep's a1-107 (open 10, close 7) with its lever net's staircase, which crossed in front of the door at z = -4, re-laid over the top: the same speed at the same size under the "nothing in front of or behind the door" rule

agent speed-2: opens in 9, closes in 7: Q spits A' at tick 5 off an odd observer pulse (a solid door opening in 9 needs an odd tick), with the lever net re-laid over the top under the "nothing in front of or behind the door" rule

agent tick-door: the open-4 machine wired to a lever: opens in 4 ticks, the proven floor for a solid door (0-ticked reach-through pullers take the top-middle block out through its corner and the center through the top cell, every input from the lever), closes in 15
